original_question: For a graph G and a graph property P, let beta_P(G) denote the maximum size of a P-matching in G, where a P-matching is a matching M whose induced subgraph <M> has property P. What Nordhaus-Gaddum type bounds can be proved for beta_P over a graph and its complement; specifically, what are the best possible lower and upper bounds for beta_P(G) + beta_P(G_bar) and for beta_P(G) * beta_P(G_bar)?
target_in_paper: The unnumbered open problem in the paper’s concluding/open-problems discussion asking for Nordhaus-Gaddum type bounds for the generalized P-matching number β_P.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core object from the paper’s framework: for a graph property P, β_P(G) is the maximum size of a matching M such that the induced subgraph on the vertices saturated by M has property P. It also correctly identifies the two standard Nordhaus-Gaddum quantities to optimize, namely β_P(G)+β_P(\overline{G}) and β_P(G)β_P(\overline{G}).
missing_details: A Nordhaus-Gaddum problem is posed for graphs of fixed order n; the question should explicitly range over all finite simple graphs G on n vertices.
The induced subgraph should be written as G[M] (or explicitly described as the subgraph induced by the vertices incident with the edges of M), matching the paper’s notation and context.
The complement \overline{G} should be specified as the usual complement on the same vertex set.
The paper’s intent is to ask for sharp/best-possible bounds as functions of n; without fixing n, the problem is not stand-alone.
It helps to state that P is an arbitrary graph property within the generalized P-matching framework; the paper does not impose extra hypotheses such as heredity or monotonicity in the formulation.
The optimization domain should be explicit: determine both lower and upper sharp bounds for the sum and for the product over all n-vertex graphs.
No ambient algebraic data (field, ring, homogeneity, nilpotency, etc.) are relevant here; the missing details are entirely graph-theoretic.
refined_question: Let P be a graph property, and for a finite simple graph G of order n let β_P(G) denote the maximum cardinality of a matching M such that the induced subgraph G[M] on the vertices incident with the edges of M has property P. Determine the sharp Nordhaus-Gaddum bounds for β_P; that is, for each positive integer n, determine the best possible lower and upper bounds, over all graphs G on n vertices, for β_P(G)+β_P(\overline{G}) and for β_P(G)β_P(\overline{G}).
justification: The draft is very close to the paper’s intent: the survey is explicitly about generalized P-matchings, using the standard β_P notation, and one of its concluding open directions is to formulate the Nordhaus-Gaddum problem for this parameter. The main gap is that the paper-faithful Nordhaus-Gaddum formulation is over the class of graphs of fixed order n, asking for sharp extremal bounds as functions of n. Tightening the quantifiers and restoring the paper’s induced-subgraph notation G[M] makes the question mathematically stand-alone and closer to the survey’s actual framing.
